plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 5.2.9
plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating the disk method for computing the volume of a solid of revolution. Panel (a): the 2D xy-plane showing region R bounded above by the curve y = f(x), below by the x-axis, and between x = a and x = b; a rotation arrow at x = b indicates revolution about the x-axis. Panel (b): a 3D perspective of the resulting solid; at a generic position x along the axis, a circular disk cross-section is highlighted in blue with radius f(x) labeled, showing that each cross-section perpendicular to the x-axis is a disk of area pi[f(x)]^2. The figure derives the disk method formula V = integral from a to b of pi[f(x)]^2 dx by identifying the cross-sectional area at each x and integrating along the axis of revolution.

elements: x-axis (horizontal, arrowhead at right) spanning the revolution interval
y-axis (vertical, arrowhead at top) at the left origin
curve y = f(x) drawn above the x-axis from x=a to x=b
shaded region R bounded above by y=f(x), below by the x-axis, between x=a and x=b (light blue fill)
vertical segment at x=a closing the left side of R
vertical segment at x=b closing the right side of R
tick labels a, b on the x-axis and a moving tick label x
circular rotation arrow around the x-axis near x=b indicating revolution about the x-axis
3D solid of revolution surface (lathe of f about the x-axis) with open elliptical rims at x=a and x=b
highlighted circular disk cross-section perpendicular to the x-axis at the current position x (light-blue fill, blue rim)
radius line from the axis point (x,0) up to the surface point (x, f(x)) on the disk
red marker dot at the disk center on the axis (x,0)
brace/label f(x) annotating the disk radius
readout of disk area pi[f(x)]^2 at the current x

interactions.label: Region & bounds
interactions.teaches: The disk radius at every position equals f(x), so editing the formula or the bounds instantly reshapes both the 2D region R and the 3D solid — the entire profile of the solid is determined by the single function f

interactions.label: Slice position x
interactions.teaches: Sweeping x moves the perpendicular disk along the axis; its radius tracks f(x) and the displayed area pi[f(x)]^2 is exactly the integrand of the volume formula V = integral pi[f(x)]^2 dx

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Switching between the revolved solid and its generating planar region R makes the construction explicit: rotating the area under y=f(x) about the x-axis produces the solid whose cross-sections are disks

demo_steps.title: The solid and one disk
demo_steps.narration: With f(x)=sqrt(x) on [0.5, 4], the solid of revolution is shown with a highlighted disk at x=2. Its radius equals f(2)≈1.41, so the cross-sectional area is pi·f(2)^2≈2·pi.

demo_steps.title: See the generating region
demo_steps.narration: Toggle to the 2D view: the same curve bounds region R above the x-axis. This is the area that, revolved about the x-axis, sweeps out the solid just seen.

demo_steps.title: Sweep the slice to b
demo_steps.narration: Back in 3D, drag x toward b=4. The disk grows as f(x) increases, illustrating why each slice contributes pi[f(x)]^2 dx and the total volume is their integral.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: map the x-interval to world X in [0, 5] (a≈0.5, b≈4 by default); vertical/radial scale so f(b)=sqrt(4)=2 maps to ~2 world units (Y up and radial). Region R fill light blue #bfe3f2 with curve stroke #2a9fd6 (~0.05 wide). Solid surface a semi-opaque lathe (light grey/white, opacity ~0.35) with black profile silhouette curves top and bottom and elliptical rims at a and b. Highlighted disk: CircleGeometry fill #bfe3f2 (opacity ~0.85) rim #2a9fd6, oriented perpendicular to X at current x. Radius line black from (x,0,0) to (x,f(x),0); center dot red #d02020 sphere ~0.06. f(x) brace/label black near the radius. Rotation arrow at b a thin torus-arc with arrowhead around X. Clamp sliceX to [a,b] at runtime; recompute lathe profile and disk radius whenever fx/a/b change. Volume integrand pi[f(x)]^2 displayed as live text.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the solid with THREE.LatheGeometry from ~120 samples of f over [a,b]; LatheGeometry revolves about Y by default, so rotate the mesh -90° about Z to align the revolution axis with world X. Recompute the lathe profile, region shape, and disk radius reactively on every equation_input parse; catch parse errors inline and keep the last valid geometry. Keep both 2D and 3D groups in the scene and show/hide on the viewMode toggle rather than rebuilding. Render the disk as a double-sided circle so it reads correctly from both sides during orbit.

authoredContext:
Let f be continuous and nonnegative on [a, b], and let R be the region that is bounded above by y = f (x), below by the x-axis, and on the sides by the lines x = a and x = b (Figure 5.2.9a). Find the volume of the solid of revolution that is generated by revolving the region R about the x-axis. We can solve this problem by slicing. For this purpose, observe that the cross section
of the solid taken perpendicular to the x-axis at the point x is a circular disk of radius f (x)
(Figure 5.2.9b). The area of this region is
A(x) = π[f (x)]
